name: Gazing into a Clear Sky

dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: ākāśaṃ vimalam paśyan kṛtvā dṛṣṭiṃ nirantarām | stabdhātmā tatkṣaṇād devi bhairavaṃ vapur āpnuyāt ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: Looking at the clear sky with an uninterrupted gaze, becoming utterly still, in that very instant, O Goddess, one attains the form of Bhairava.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: becoming still means the sense of the body vanishes and thoughts and emotions are arrested; the vastness of the sky lets the viewer be lost in a sense of infinity; 'fixed eyes' means without blinking. Singh classes it as śāmbhavopāya. Wallis: 'sky-gazing'.
dharana.instruction: Rest a steady gaze in a clear sky, away from the sun, and become still.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 61' = verse 84 (agrees with Singh)
The Mystery Within (2019), parallel translations: 'Dharana 61 • verso 84' (agrees)
Wallis concordance: verse 84 = 'Sky-gazing (Y60 ~ C1)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 84 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position with a clear view of open sky; lying on the back outdoors works well.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 84 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a clear sky filling the field of view, with nothing for the eye to hold on to.
geometry.svg_hint: an empty pale-blue field with no marks
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Lost in the sky
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the eye rests in a boundless sky and the sense of a small, bounded self falls away. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Let the gaze rest in a clear sky
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.gaze: Eyes open and soft on clear sky, well away from the sun; blink freely
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: A clear, cloudless sky, seen without interruption
attention.secondary: The stillness that comes with it

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Looking at the clear sky with an uninterrupted gaze, becoming utterly still, in that very instant, O Goddess, one attains the form of Bhairava.
adiyogi.method_summary: Lie or sit where you can see a clear sky, well away from the sun. Let the gaze rest in it steadily and become still. Let the vastness take attention. Blink whenever needed.

honesty.disclosure: Door 061 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 61 (verse 84) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 061 is dharana 61, verse 84. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.
School adjustment: Singh reads 'fixed eyes' as without blinking; this school keeps the steady gaze and allows normal blinking.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Never look at or near the sun. Blink whenever needed: the classical gaze is unblinking, but this school does not ask for it. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 061: gazing into a clear sky. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 61, verse 84.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit or lie where you can see clear sky. The map is open sky filling the view.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Sit or lie comfortably. Eyes open and soft on clear sky. Never on the sun.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Let the gaze rest steadily in the sky, well away from the sun. Become still. Let the vastness take you. Blink when you need to.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: a bounded self dissolving into sky. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 84: looking at the clear sky with an unbroken gaze, utterly still, in that instant one attains the form of Bhairava.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Release the attention. Feel the weight of the body on its support. Open the eyes when ready.
